49: // MatchExpression matches requests by evaluating a

121: // Provision sets ups m.
122: func (m *MatchExpression) Provision(ctx caddy.Context) error {
123: 	m.log = ctx.Logger()
124: 
125: 	// replace placeholders with a function call - this is just some
126: 	// light (and possibly naïve) syntactic sugar
127: 	m.expandedExpr = placeholderRegexp.ReplaceAllString(m.Expr, placeholderExpansion)
128: 
129: 	// our type adapter expands CEL's standard type support
130: 	m.ta = celTypeAdapter{}
131: 
132: 	// initialize the CEL libraries from the Matcher implementations which
133: 	// have been configured to support CEL.
134: 	matcherLibProducers := []CELLibraryProducer{}
135: 	for _, info := range caddy.GetModules("http.matchers") {
136: 		p, ok := info.New().(CELLibraryProducer)
137: 		if ok {
138: 			matcherLibProducers = append(matcherLibProducers, p)
139: 		}
140: 	}
141: 
142: 	// add the matcher name to the context so that the matcher name
143: 	// can be used by regexp matchers being provisioned
144: 	ctx = ctx.WithValue(MatcherNameCtxKey, m.Name)
145: 
146: 	// Assemble the compilation and program options from the different library
147: 	// producers into a single cel.Library implementation.
148: 	matcherEnvOpts := []cel.EnvOption{}
149: 	matcherProgramOpts := []cel.ProgramOption{}
150: 	for _, producer := range matcherLibProducers {
151: 		l, err := producer.CELLibrary(ctx)
152: 		if err != nil {
153: 			return fmt.Errorf("error initializing CEL library for %T: %v", producer, err)
154: 		}
155: 		matcherEnvOpts = append(matcherEnvOpts, l.CompileOptions()...)
156: 		matcherProgramOpts = append(matcherProgramOpts, l.ProgramOptions()...)
157: 	}
158: 	matcherLib := cel.Lib(NewMatcherCELLibrary(matcherEnvOpts, matcherProgramOpts))
159: 
160: 	// create the CEL environment
161: 	env, err := cel.NewEnv(
162: 		cel.Function(placeholderFuncName, cel.SingletonBinaryBinding(m.caddyPlaceholderFunc), cel.Overload(
163: 			placeholderFuncName+"_httpRequest_string",
164: 			[]*cel.Type{httpRequestObjectType, cel.StringType},
165: 			cel.AnyType,
166: 		)),
167: 		cel.Variable("request", httpRequestObjectType),
168: 		cel.CustomTypeAdapter(m.ta),
169: 		ext.Strings(),
170: 		matcherLib,
171: 	)
172: 	if err != nil {
173: 		return fmt.Errorf("setting up CEL environment: %v", err)
174: 	}
175: 
176: 	// parse and type-check the expression
177: 	checked, issues := env.Compile(m.expandedExpr)
178: 	if issues.Err() != nil {
179: 		return fmt.Errorf("compiling CEL program: %s", issues.Err())
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	// request matching is a boolean operation, so we don't really know
183: 	// what to do if the expression returns a non-boolean type
184: 	if checked.OutputType() != cel.BoolType {
185: 		return fmt.Errorf("CEL request matcher expects return type of bool, not %s", checked.OutputType())
186: 	}
187: 
188: 	// compile the "program"
189: 	m.prg, err = env.Program(checked, cel.EvalOptions(cel.OptOptimize))
190: 	if err != nil {
191: 		return fmt.Errorf("compiling CEL program: %s", err)
192: 	}
193: 	return nil
194: }

197: func (m MatchExpression) Match(r *http.Request) bool {

201: 		m.log.Error("evaluating expression", zap.Error(err))
202: 		SetVar(r.Context(), MatcherErrorVarKey, err)
203: 		return false
204: 	}
205: 	if outBool, ok := out.Value().(bool); ok {
206: 		return outBool
207: 	}
208: 	return false
209: }

349: // implementation as a first class function within the CEL expression
350: // matcher.

352: 	// CELLibrary creates a cel.Library which makes it possible to use the
353: 	// target object within CEL expression matchers.

357: // CELMatcherImpl creates a new cel.Library based on the following pieces of
358: // data:
359: //
360: //   - macroName: the function name to be used within CEL. This will be a macro
361: //     and not a function proper.
362: //   - funcName: the function overload name generated by the CEL macro used to
363: //     represent the matcher.
364: //   - matcherDataTypes: the argument types to the macro.
365: //   - fac: a matcherFactory implementation which converts from CEL constant
366: //     values to a Matcher instance.
367: //
368: // Note, macro names and function names must not collide with other macros or
369: // functions exposed within CEL expressions, or an error will be produced
370: // during the expression matcher plan time.
371: //
372: // The existing CELMatcherImpl support methods are configured to support a
373: // limited set of function signatures. For strong type validation you may need
374: // to provide a custom macro which does a more detailed analysis of the CEL
375: // literal provided to the macro as an argument.
376: func CELMatcherImpl(macroName, funcName string, matcherDataTypes []*cel.Type, fac CELMatcherFactory) (cel.Library, error) {
377: 	requestType := cel.ObjectType("http.Request")
378: 	var macro parser.Macro
379: 	switch len(matcherDataTypes) {
380: 	case 1:
381: 		matcherDataType := matcherDataTypes[0]
382: 		switch matcherDataType.String() {
383: 		case "list(string)":
384: 			macro = parser.NewGlobalVarArgMacro(macroName, celMatcherStringListMacroExpander(funcName))
385: 		case cel.StringType.String():
386: 			macro = parser.NewGlobalMacro(macroName, 1, celMatcherStringMacroExpander(funcName))
387: 		case CELTypeJSON.String():
388: 			macro = parser.NewGlobalMacro(macroName, 1, celMatcherJSONMacroExpander(funcName))
389: 		default:
390: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported matcher data type: %s", matcherDataType)
391: 		}
392: 	case 2:
393: 		if matcherDataTypes[0] == cel.StringType && matcherDataTypes[1] == cel.StringType {
394: 			macro = parser.NewGlobalMacro(macroName, 2, celMatcherStringListMacroExpander(funcName))
395: 			matcherDataTypes = []*cel.Type{cel.ListType(cel.StringType)}
396: 		} else {
397: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported matcher data type: %s, %s", matcherDataTypes[0], matcherDataTypes[1])
398: 		}
399: 	case 3:
400: 		if matcherDataTypes[0] == cel.StringType && matcherDataTypes[1] == cel.StringType && matcherDataTypes[2] == cel.StringType {
401: 			macro = parser.NewGlobalMacro(macroName, 3, celMatcherStringListMacroExpander(funcName))
402: 			matcherDataTypes = []*cel.Type{cel.ListType(cel.StringType)}
403: 		} else {
404: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported matcher data type: %s, %s, %s", matcherDataTypes[0], matcherDataTypes[1], matcherDataTypes[2])
405: 		}
406: 	}
407: 	envOptions := []cel.EnvOption{
408: 		cel.Macros(macro),
409: 		cel.Function(funcName,
410: 			cel.Overload(funcName, append([]*cel.Type{requestType}, matcherDataTypes...), cel.BoolType),
411: 			cel.SingletonBinaryBinding(CELMatcherRuntimeFunction(funcName, fac))),
412: 	}
413: 	programOptions := []cel.ProgramOption{
414: 		cel.CustomDecorator(CELMatcherDecorator(funcName, fac)),
415: 	}
416: 	return NewMatcherCELLibrary(envOptions, programOptions), nil
417: }

444: // CELMatcherDecorator matches a call overload generated by a CEL macro
445: // that takes a single argument, and optimizes the implementation to precompile
446: // the matcher and return a function that references the precompiled and
447: // provisioned matcher.
448: func CELMatcherDecorator(funcName string, fac CELMatcherFactory) interpreter.InterpretableDecorator {
449: 	return func(i interpreter.Interpretable) (interpreter.Interpretable, error) {
450: 		call, ok := i.(interpreter.InterpretableCall)
451: 		if !ok {
452: 			return i, nil
453: 		}
454: 		if call.OverloadID() != funcName {
455: 			return i, nil
456: 		}
457: 		callArgs := call.Args()
458: 		reqAttr, ok := callArgs[0].(interpreter.InterpretableAttribute)
459: 		if !ok {
460: 			return nil, errors.New("missing 'request' argument")
461: 		}
462: 		nsAttr, ok := reqAttr.Attr().(interpreter.NamespacedAttribute)
463: 		if !ok {
464: 			return nil, errors.New("missing 'request' argument")
465: 		}
466: 		varNames := nsAttr.CandidateVariableNames()
467: 		if len(varNames) != 1 || len(varNames) == 1 && varNames[0] != "request" {
468: 			return nil, errors.New("missing 'request' argument")
469: 		}
470: 		matcherData, ok := callArgs[1].(interpreter.InterpretableConst)
471: 		if !ok {
472: 			// If the matcher arguments are not constant, then this means
473: 			// they contain a Caddy placeholder reference and the evaluation
474: 			// and matcher provisioning should be handled at dynamically.
475: 			return i, nil
476: 		}
477: 		matcher, err := fac(matcherData.Value())
478: 		if err != nil {
479: 			return nil, err
480: 		}
481: 		return interpreter.NewCall(
482: 			i.ID(), funcName, funcName+"_opt",
483: 			[]interpreter.Interpretable{reqAttr},
484: 			func(args ...ref.Val) ref.Val {
485: 				// The request value, guaranteed to be of type celHTTPRequest
486: 				celReq := args[0]
487: 				// If needed this call could be changed to convert the value
488: 				// to a *http.Request using CEL's ConvertToNative method.
489: 				httpReq := celReq.Value().(celHTTPRequest)
490: 				return types.Bool(matcher.Match(httpReq.Request))
491: 			},
492: 		), nil
493: 	}
494: }

496: // CELMatcherRuntimeFunction creates a function binding for when the input to the matcher
497: // is dynamically resolved rather than a set of static constant values.
498: func CELMatcherRuntimeFunction(funcName string, fac CELMatcherFactory) functions.BinaryOp {
499: 	return func(celReq, matcherData ref.Val) ref.Val {
500: 		matcher, err := fac(matcherData)
501: 		if err != nil {
502: 			return types.NewErr(err.Error())
